clue.text: Cheese nasty woman cut for author

indicators.note: cut tells us one piece is chopped away from the cheese, leaving the rest

parts.note: Gorgonzola is an Italian blue cheese
a gorgon is a fearsome, ugly woman, after the snake-haired monsters of myth

explanation.surface: Someone trims a sharp-tongued woman down to size and swaps her for a novelist, like a recipe gone strange.
explanation.walkthrough: Take GORGON out of the front of GORGONZOLA and the French novelist is left.
explanation.definitionFit: Émile Zola was a French novelist, so he is an example of a writer.

clue.text: Funny opera (not English) includes light recitative

indicators.note: includes means one piece sits inside the other, holding it
funny here means odd or peculiar, so the letters come out in a strange order
not means a letter is left out of the word opera

parts.note: to light on something is to land on it, as a bird alights

explanation.surface: A comic opera with nothing English in it still finds room for some light sung speech.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Funny' looks like a description of the opera but signals the jumble; 'not English' leaves OPRA, which 'Funny' turns into PARO before 'includes' takes the light word.
explanation.definitionFit: Parlando is a musical direction for singing in a speech-like way, which is what recitative does.

clue.text: Designer's new maternal style — see more than one Conservative wearing it

indicators.note: the pair of Tories is wearing the rest, so it wraps around them
new signals the letters of the two words are made over into a fresh order

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for Conservative, and two of them give CC

explanation.surface: A fashion house launches a fresh maternity line, and a crowd of Tory politicians is seen modelling it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' makes STELLAMARTNEY from the two words; 'wearing' puts the Tories inside. 'see' is only a link here, not a cross-reference.
explanation.definitionFit: Stella McCartney is a well-known British fashion designer, daughter of Paul McCartney.

clue.text: Cleaner covering everything in part of palace, maybe

indicators.note: covering means the cleaning tool goes round the other piece

parts.note: a broom is a sweeping tool for cleaning
all means everything

explanation.surface: A cleaner is busy covering every corner of some wing of a palace.
explanation.definitionFit: A palace may well have a grand hall for dancing, so it is an example, hence 'maybe'.

clue.text: Rang off, being emotionally disturbed?

definitions.meaning: ended a phone call by putting the receiver down

explanation.surface: Someone ends a call abruptly because they are upset.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both ended a call and, informally, troubled or fixated.

clue.text: Terrified female given instruction to slow down

parts.note: rit., short for ritardando, is the musical marking to slow down

explanation.surface: A woman who is told to take it easy is actually scared stiff.
explanation.walkthrough: FRIT is British dialect for frightened, made famous by Margaret Thatcher taunting an opponent.
explanation.definitionFit: The dialect word means frightened, which is a synonym of scared or terrified.

clue.text: Added substances clean underwear

parts.note: to do a room is to clean it
pants are underwear in British English

explanation.surface: A laundry detergent with additives is advertised for washing underwear.
explanation.definitionFit: Dopants are impurities added to a semiconductor to change its properties.

clue.text: Bird outside enclosure returned — outside a period of days

indicators.note: the bird is placed outside, so it wraps round what follows

parts.note: a jay is a bird of the crow family

indicators.note: the second outside puts the reversed pen around the little word a
returned means the word for an enclosure is read backwards

parts.note: a run is an enclosed area for animals, such as a chicken run

explanation.surface: A bird keeps circling a pen it came back to, over a span of days.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' gives NUR, and 'outside' twice nests the pieces: NUAR first, then the bird split around it.
explanation.definitionFit: The first month of the year is a stretch of thirty-one days.

clue.text: Actor as famous convert, born-again Christian?

parts.note: Saint Paul was famously converted on the road to Damascus
a convert is said to become a new man

explanation.surface: A film star is cast as a celebrated religious convert who has been born again.
explanation.definitionFit: Paul Newman was an American film actor, star of The Hustler and Cool Hand Luke.

clue.text: Some illumination in difficult situation following escape

indicators.note: following means the predicament comes after the getaway

parts.note: on the lam means on the run, so lam is an escape
a plight is a difficult situation

explanation.surface: Someone in a tight spot after a breakout is glad of a little light.
explanation.definitionFit: Light from a lamp is one source of illumination, hence 'some'.

clue.text: See 3
Porn star in dalliance, sadly without affection

indicators.note: without here means outside, so the jumbled letters wrap round the other piece
sadly signals the letters of the word dalliance are put into a sorry new order

parts.note: love is affection

explanation.surface: A sex-film actor engages in a fling that is sadly loveless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside here, not lacking: 'sadly' makes LINDALACE, which wraps the affection.
explanation.definitionFit: Linda Lovelace was the actress who starred in the 1972 adult film Deep Throat.

clue.text: Exotic dance movement with which girl wins Bruno's heart

indicators.note: the girl wins, that is gains, the next piece added on

parts.note: a lass is a girl

indicators.note: heart means the central letter of the name Bruno

explanation.surface: A young woman captures the heart of a man called Bruno with an exotic dance.
explanation.definitionFit: The lassu is the slow opening section of the Hungarian csárdás dance.

clue.text: Spooner's slog, woman for taming being a dull person

indicators.note: Spooner's means swap the opening sounds of the two words, as Reverend Spooner did

parts.note: to plod is to slog on wearily
Kate is the shrew in Shakespeare's The Taming of the Shrew

explanation.surface: A drudge and a woman in need of taming make a dull character.
explanation.walkthrough: Swapping the first sounds of PLOD and KATE gives CLOD PATE; the K sound is spelt C.
explanation.definitionFit: A clodpate is an old word for a blockhead or dimwit.

clue.text: Engineers with crazy guy set up electronic device

indicators.note: set up in a down clue means the pieces read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, the British Army corps
a nut is a crazy person

explanation.surface: Army engineers and an eccentric build a piece of electronics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set up' turns RENUT into TUNER, reading upwards in a down light.
explanation.definitionFit: A tuner is a radio component or device that selects a broadcast frequency.

clue.text: Capital performance by one half confused

indicators.note: only half the word is muddled, so its first pair of letters swap

parts.note: a solo is a performance by one person

explanation.surface: A one-person show in the capital goes half wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half confused' swaps the first half SO to OS, leaving LO alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Oslo is the capital city of Norway.

clue.text: Biblical king given greeting with more than just a shofar, seemingly

parts.note: hi is a greeting

parts.words: more than just a shofar, seemingly
parts.note: a shofar is a ram's horn, so more than the horn is the whole beast

explanation.surface: An Old Testament ruler is welcomed with a blast on a ceremonial horn and more.
explanation.walkthrough: A shofar is the ram's-horn trumpet blown in Jewish ritual.
explanation.definitionFit: Hiram, king of Tyre, sent cedar and craftsmen to Solomon in the Bible.

clue.text: Horses apt to bolt, abandoning a warm Leopardstown enclosure?

indicators.note: horses that bolt run off wildly, so the letters scatter
abandoning means the letter named after it is left out

explanation.surface: Horses ready to break loose leave a racecourse paddock behind.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove A from HORSES APT and 'to bolt' rearranges the rest. Leopardstown is an Irish racecourse; the Irish call an airing cupboard a hot press, a joking enclosure.
explanation.definitionFit: In Ireland an airing cupboard is a heated cupboard; the clue jokes it is an enclosure.

clue.text: Wild animal's connections being read out

indicators.note: read out means spoken, so we want a word that sounds like another

parts.note: links are connections

explanation.surface: Someone reads aloud a list of family ties of some wild creature.
explanation.definitionFit: The lynx is a wild cat with tufted ears.

clue.text: See 12 across
Try to be more charming? Not I, if you do this!

parts.note: read the pieces as an instruction: turn the two words it on round, and you get these words

explanation.surface: Someone is advised to lay on the charm, but refuses, saying not they.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as wordplay: TURN, a reversal signal, then IT ON, which turned round gives NOT I.
explanation.definitionFit: To lay on the charm is a common idiom for making oneself appealing.

clue.text: See 9
Separate river drying up before the end

indicators.note: the river runs dry just short of its finish, so its final letter goes

parts.note: the Severn is Britain's longest river

explanation.surface: A river splits off and runs dry before reaching its mouth.
explanation.definitionFit: To sever is to cut apart or divide, a synonym of separate as a verb.

clue.text: One of five children in street seen in a glance

indicators.note: in places the child inside the abbreviation for street

parts.note: a quin is one of quintuplets, five children born together

explanation.surface: A quintuplet is glimpsed briefly out in the road.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang, having a squint means taking a quick look.

clue.text: Introductory enquiry — who played what sounds like rugby, briefly?

indicators.note: played signals the three letters of the word who are rearranged
sounds like means the next piece is spoken aloud

parts.note: RU is short for Rugby Union

explanation.surface: A newcomer starts by asking who has played a sport that seems like rugby.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters R and U said aloud make the phrase 'are you'.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is the standard opening question when greeting someone.

clue.text: Someone funny and passionate with extra love

indicators.note: the extra letter is slipped in among the existing ones

parts.note: hot means passionate
love is zero in tennis, which looks like the letter O

explanation.surface: A comic who is also an ardent lover is a great catch.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoot is an informal word for a very amusing person.

clue.text: Rude wife assumed command going about

indicators.note: going about means surrounding, so the past tense of lead goes round

parts.note: to have led is to have taken charge

explanation.surface: An ill-mannered wife takes charge and bosses everyone around.
explanation.definitionFit: Lewd means vulgar or obscene, one sense of rude.

clue.text: Watery stuff from two rivers being baled out of rowing boat

indicators.note: bailing water from a boat removes it, so these letters come out

parts.note: a wherry is a light rowing boat
R is the abbreviation for river, two of them give RR

explanation.surface: Water from two rivers is scooped out of a little rowing boat.
explanation.definitionFit: Whey is the thin liquid left after milk curdles, so it is watery stuff.

clue.text: Squelchy tropical fish ship collected

indicators.note: the fish collected the ship, taking it inside

parts.note: the moray is a tropical eel
SS stands for steamship

explanation.surface: A tropical fish is gathered up from a ship, soggy and slimy.
explanation.definitionFit: Boggy ground is a morass, so marshy ground is squelchy underfoot.

clue.text: Underwear back to front one king removed for a laugh

indicators.note: removed means one letter is taken away
back to front sends the final letter round to the start

parts.note: knickers are women's underpants
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: Underpants put on back to front, minus a king, are good for a laugh.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back to front' moves the final S of KNICKERS to the front, giving SKNICKER; removing one K leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A snicker is a smothered half-laugh, a synonym of snigger.
